# Signatories and community support

Shaurita D. Hutchins and Samuel Bharti are PhD candidates at the University of Alabama at Birmingham and will co-lead the project.

**Hutchins will lead educational design and community development.** She will develop the tutorial specification and accessibility guidance, coordinate the example tutorials, and establish the contribution process. Her training is in genetics, genomics, and bioinformatics, and her work combines computational biology with reproducible R/Bioconductor workflows. She brings experience in open-source training and Carpentries instruction. Her [Prioritizing Candidate Genetic Variants Using GTEx, HuBMAP, and IDG](https://cfdetrainingcenter.github.io/candidate-genetic-variants/) module for the CFDE Training Center includes coding activities that run in the browser and knowledge checks.

**Bharti will lead software architecture and engine integration.** He will develop the adapters and common validation reports, and connect the package to existing engine checks. His teaching work includes [r-for-beginners](https://github.com/samuelbharti/r-for-beginners), an adaptation of Software Carpentry lessons with slides. He also develops the R packages bioclients, biohttp, and biobouncer, and publishes package documentation through GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages.

We will jointly design the package API and registry, agree on governance, and develop the example tutorials.

We requested public feedback through [r/Stats](https://www.reddit.com/r/Stats/comments/1wvj3wd/for_people_who_teach_or_learn_r_how_do_you_find/) and the [learnr webR discussion](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/issues/766#issuecomment-5944771998). Community contributor [\@coatless](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/issues/766#issuecomment-5944898742) directed us to learnr2 and Quarto Live, prompting us to focus on shared metadata and checks. Their response addressed related tools, rather than reviewing the proposed schema. We will seek specific feedback on the schema and adapter boundaries from engine maintainers.

We will also consult Carpentries and Bioconductor educators and university and community instructors, adding documented feedback and letters of support as received.
